findings.checklist_item: [ ] Specify in Scope how spawn_detached handles per-caller env: expose an env/env-projection parameter so push.py keeps its project_child_env secret-strip and REBAR_SYNC_PUSH, and confirm the PYTHONPATH bootstrap composes on top of a caller-supplied env.
evidence: push.py:204 child_env = _child_env.project_child_env(os.environ, relationship="unrelated"); push.py:205 child_env["REBAR_SYNC_PUSH"] = "always"
enrich_drain.py:427 child_env = {**os.environ}; compact_trigger.py:226 child_env = {**os.environ}

Plan lists what spawn_detached 'would own' as: PYTHONPATH bootstrap, detach flags, durable cwd, never-raise posture — env projection is absent from both the 'owns' list and the 'callers supply only' list
findings.finding: The helper interface ('callers would supply only the child entry point and their stderr sink') omits per-site child-env construction, which differs materially: push.py projects os.environ via project_child_env(relationship='unrelated') to STRIP Jira secrets (JIRA_API_TOKEN/JIRA_PAT) and sets REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always, while the drain/sweep pass a plain {**os.environ}. A helper that owns env construction without exposing this per-caller could drop push.py's secret-stripping (a leak) or under-serve the sweep/drain.
findings.location: Scope, first bullet ('callers would supply only the child entry point and their stderr sink')
scenarios: Consolidation folds push.py onto a helper that constructs a plain child env, silently dropping the secret-strip and leaking JIRA_API_TOKEN into a git-push child
Helper cannot express REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always without a caller-supplied env hook
findings.suggested_fix: Add a caller-supplied `env` (or `env_projection`) parameter to the spawn_detached signature; document that push.py passes the secret-stripped projected env and the helper only layers PYTHONPATH onto whatever env the caller provides.

findings.checklist_item: [ ] Reconcile the divergent detach-flag and never-raise behavior across the three sites: state whether spawn_detached's owned Windows branch and broad-except now apply to the push path, and confirm that is intended (or preserve push.py's OSError-only / no-Windows posture).
evidence: push.py:227-229 start_new_session=True / close_fds=True with no creationflags branch; push.py:230 except OSError as exc
enrich_drain.py:410-418 _detach_kwargs with an os.name=='nt' creationflags branch; enrich_drain.py:462 except Exception
compact_trigger.py:207-213 _detach_kwargs mirroring the drain; compact_trigger.py:260 except Exception
findings.finding: The plan says spawn_detached 'would own ... the detach flags' and 'the never-raise posture', but the three sites diverge on both, and the plan does not reconcile the resulting behavior change. push.py has NO Windows/creationflags branch (it inlines start_new_session/close_fds), whereas drain/sweep supply Windows DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW via _detach_kwargs; and push.py's never-raise wrapper catches only OSError while the other two catch broad Exception (with different log wording). A single owned implementation changes push.py's platform behavior and exception surface.
findings.location: Scope, first bullet ('the detach flags ... and the never-raise posture')
scenarios: Consolidated helper adds Windows creationflags to the push path, which was previously POSIX-only by omission — unvetted new behavior
Consolidated broad-except changes push.py from catching OSError to swallowing all exceptions, or vice-versa, altering which failures surface

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how AC2 is enforced (e.g. a static/AST or `grep -E` ban-test that fails if `subprocess.Popen(` with detach flags appears outside `_proc.spawn_detached`, or an import-graph assertion), not just 'a test pins it'.
evidence: 'A test pins that every detached spawn goes through it, so a fourth site cannot reintroduce the class by copy-paste.'
No approach stated: a runtime test cannot easily observe 'every spawn site'; enforcement is typically a static/AST/grep ban-test or a lint rule, which the plan does not name.
findings.finding: AC2 asserts 'a test pins that every detached spawn goes through it' but does not describe the mechanism by which a test can prove no fourth site re-implements the bootstrap; the enforcement approach is the novel de-duplication guarantee and is left unspecified.
scenarios: An executor writes a test that only exercises the three known sites at runtime, which does not actually prevent a fourth copy-paste site from existing.
Ambiguity forces a clarifying question about how the invariant is enforced.
findings.suggested_fix: State the enforcement mechanism, e.g. a test that greps the tree for detach-flag/Popen usage outside `_proc.py` and asserts the only match is inside `spawn_detached`, anchored so a fourth site fails CI.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the pinning test distinguishes DETACHED (outlives-parent) spawns from the two synchronous reap-and-wait Popen sites (acli_subprocess.py:63, wiki_render.py:390) that legitimately keep their own start_new_session=True and are NOT expected to route through spawn_detached.
evidence: search hit: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:63 'Popen(start_new_session=True)'

search hit: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py:390 'start_new_session=True' — verified as a synchronous pandoc child reaped on timeout, reads from stdin (stdin=PIPE), not detached
_proc.py:1-15 module docstring names these two as the reap_process_group callers ('the grounding harness ... and the reconciler's ACLI transport')
findings.finding: The AC's pinning test ('every detached spawn goes through it, so a fourth site cannot reintroduce the class') will collide with two existing same-idiom sites that are NOT detached spawns and must not be collapsed: adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:63 and adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py:390 both use subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True) but are synchronous reap-and-wait children (via reap_process_group), not children that outlive the parent. A naive test keyed on the start_new_session=True idiom would falsely flag these two legitimate reap-side consumers of _proc.py.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, line 2 ('A test pins that every detached spawn goes through it'); Scope bullet 1 (_proc.py 'already home to reap_process_group')
scenarios: The pinning test greps for start_new_session=True / creationflags and asserts each call site imports spawn_detached — it then fails on the two reap-only sites that legitimately keep their own Popen.
A future reviewer trusts a green test that actually excludes the reap sites by an under-specified rule and a real fourth detached site slips through the same exclusion.

findings.finding: The plan bundles two arguably-separable concerns: (1) consolidating the three detached-spawn sites behind one helper (the title), and (2) recording/implementing a decision on `_config_sources.repo_root`'s cwd fallback for long-lived IN-PROCESS callers (daemon threads that, per the plan, 'no longer reach it now that they get an explicit cwd' — i.e. orthogonal to the detached-spawn seam). The plan itself notes the detached children no longer hit this path, so the repo_root posture is a distinct reason-to-change from the spawn consolidation.
findings.location: Scope — 'Related open question' bullet; AC line 4 (repo_root decision)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that behaviorally verifies spawn_detached applies the durable cwd, the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, and the platform detach flags (e.g. a test spawning a real child that asserts its effective cwd and successful rebar import), not only the structural single-source-of-truth pin.
evidence: AC2: 'A test pins that every detached spawn goes through it, so a fourth site cannot reintroduce the class by copy-paste.'
AC5: 'make lint, make typecheck and CI's pytest invocation are green.'

The provenance is a property (cwd) that was silently missing at all three sites; consolidation is the fix, but nothing in the ACs verifies the helper actually carries cwd/bootstrap/detach-flags through to a spawned child.
findings.finding: The AC pins that 'every detached spawn goes through' the helper (a structural anti-copy-paste guard) but no acceptance criterion asserts that `spawn_detached` BEHAVIORALLY reproduces the properties the three sites depend on — the durable cwd (the 3198 fix), the PYTHONPATH bootstrap that lets a bare-python child import rebar, and the platform detach flags. Since the helper is newly-authored code that centralizes these, a purely structural pin plus 'make lint/typecheck/pytest green' can pass even if the consolidated helper silently drops one of these properties (the same class of omission as 3198).
